Inference for selector via bootstrapping

infer_boot.Rd

Inference for selector via bootstrapping

Usage

infer_boot(
  object,
  data,
  inference_target = c("selections", "all"),
  pad = c("zero_side", "none", "all"),
  conf.level = 0.95,
  type = c("paired", "residual"),
  B = 250,
  cluster = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

a selector object

data

the data used to fit the selector

inference_target

is inference requested on all or selected only

pad

how to pad the bootstrap percentile intervals, which otherwise collapse toward [0, 0] for small nonzero coefficients the selector rarely picks. Within each replicate a non-selected coefficient is 0.

  • "zero_side" (default): an interval that contains 0 has each endpoint pushed out to at least -delta / delta; intervals that exclude 0 are unchanged. [-delta, delta] is a region of "reasonably confident null", which tends to shrink as n grows.

  • "none": the raw percentile interval ("confident nulls").

  • "all": every interval is widened by delta on both sides.

The radius delta is set from the selector (scaled metric) and returned in the null_radius column of tidy(). The column is left out when no interval could be padded (pad = "none", or a radius of 0):

  • select_ncvreg(): gamma * lambda_eff for MCP/SCAD with "zero_side", lambda_eff with "all" (see select_ncvreg() resampling below).

  • select_glmnet(): lambda; lasso select_ncvreg(): lambda_eff. The lasso's bias does not vanish for large effects, so "zero_side" warns. "all", which also widens intervals that exclude 0, is the alternative to consider.

  • select_stepwise_ic(): sqrt(k) times the full-model standard error, with k = 2 (AIC) or log(n) (BIC). Requires n > p + 1.

  • select_full_model() / select_null_model(): 0, so no padding.

The radii are motivated by the gaussian family in an orthonormal design; other families warn.

For select_ncvreg(), every resample is refit at lambda_eff, the smallest penalty giving the selected model (see select_ncvreg()), rather than at the cross-validated penalty, which can sit near the smallest selected effect rather than the noise level (see GitHub issue #34). So estimate can differ from coef for a coefficient in MCP's shrinkage zone. lambda_eff is reported in the inferrer's meta.

A resample whose path ends before lambda_eff (a binomial fit that saturates, e.g. under separation, or one that reaches a dfmax passed to select_ncvreg()) is fit at the smallest penalty it reached, which shrinks it more; their number is reported in a warning and as n_short_path in the meta.

Warnings from fitting the resamples (e.g. from glm() or ncvreg()) are collected and given once each, with the number of resamples that raised them, with or without a cluster. lambda_eff is motivated by MCP and SCAD; with the lasso it is used too, with a warning when it is below the cross-validated penalty.

conf.level

.95 by default

type

the bootstrap type. Only "paired" (resampling rows) is implemented; "residual" is reserved and currently an error.

B

number of bootstrap resamples

cluster

NULL (default) to fit the resamples sequentially, or a cluster from parallel::makeCluster() to fit them in parallel. Setting up and stopping the cluster is left to you, so one cluster can serve several calls. Each resample draws from its own L'Ecuyer-CMRG stream (parallel::nextRNGStream(), as with doRNG or future.apply's future.seed = TRUE), started from your session's random number state, so for a given set.seed() the results are the same with or without a cluster and with any number of workers. The session's generator is left as it was, with its stream advanced by one draw, and each worker's random number state is restored when infer_boot() returns. Each worker must have selectInferToolkit installed (a fork cluster from parallel::makeForkCluster() shares the calling session's instead). The progress bar is shown either way; see pbapply::pboptions() to turn it off.

...

not used. Any argument passed here is an error, so that a misspelled or removed argument (such as debias) can't be silently ignored.

Value

an inferrer object; see tidy.inferrer(). Its inferences include prop_selected (the proportion of resamples in which each term was selected) and, when intervals are padded, null_radius (the padding radius; see pad).

Examples

set.seed(1)
sel <- select_ncvreg(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars)
set.seed(2)
inf <- infer_boot(sel, data = mtcars, B = 50)
#> Bootstrapping with B = 50 replicates...
tidy(inf)
#> # A tibble: 11 × 8
#>    term        selected  coef estimate ci_low ci_high prop_selected null_radius
#>    <chr>          <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>         <dbl>       <dbl>
#>  1 (Intercept)        1 20.1    20.1    19.0    20.9           1          NA   
#>  2 cyl                0  0      NA      NA      NA            NA           1.02
#>  3 disp               0  0      NA      NA      NA            NA           1.02
#>  4 hp                 0  0      NA      NA      NA            NA           1.02
#>  5 drat               0  0      NA      NA      NA            NA           1.02
#>  6 wt                 1 -3.83   -3.38   -6.15    1.02          0.9         1.02
#>  7 qsec               1  2.19    1.35   -1.02    4.56          0.58        1.02
#>  8 vs                 0  0      NA      NA      NA            NA           1.02
#>  9 am                 1  1.46    0.588  -1.02    2.42          0.4         1.02
#> 10 gear               0  0      NA      NA      NA            NA           1.02
#> 11 carb               0  0      NA      NA      NA            NA           1.02

# \donttest{
# In parallel: make the cluster once, reuse it, and stop it when done
cl <- parallel::makeCluster(2)
set.seed(2)
inf_par <- infer_boot(sel, data = mtcars, B = 50, cluster = cl)
#> Bootstrapping with B = 50 replicates...
parallel::stopCluster(cl)
all.equal(tidy(inf), tidy(inf_par)) # same resamples, same results
#> [1] TRUE
# }
